title: Record keeping, audit, grievance and public communication
objectives: List the records, audit and grievance duties of a research analyst.
Apply the rules on public appearances and social media.
body_md:
## Duties beyond the report

| Duty | Rule in outline (verify current text) |
|---|---|
| **Records** | Keep research reports, recommendations, client agreements, fee receipts and communications for **5 years** |
| **Annual audit** | Compliance audit of the registration conditions by a qualified professional |
| **Compliance officer** | Designated person for filings and complaints |
| **Grievances** | Handle complaints promptly; escalate via **SEBI SCORES** and the **SMART ODR** portal |
| **Disclosures** | Registration number, holdings, compensation, conflicts and the market-risk caution in every report |

## Public appearances and social media

- Disclose holdings and conflicts at the time of the appearance, in the same format as in reports.
- Advertisements must be fair, must not promise returns and must carry registration details and the standard caution.
- Do not claim SEBI **approval**: SEBI registers, it does not endorse.
- Messages sent to many people (channels, groups) are **publications** and need the same disclosures.

## Fees

Fee limits for individual and HUF clients and the rules on fee collection come from the regulations and circulars; check the current cap before quoting any figure.

## Practical routine

Maintain a **disclosure checklist**, a **log of client communication**, and a **calendar** for the audit and renewal.

> **Exam tip:** Retain records for five years and never describe registration as SEBI approval.
example: An analyst posts a stock target on social media. Without holdings and registration disclosures this breaches the code, even if the target is sound.
say: Here are my registration number and my holdings in this stock.
SEBI registers analysts; it does not endorse their views.
never: I am SEBI approved, so my calls are safe.
A group post is not a recommendation.

check.why: The regulations require a five-year retention period (verify current text).
